_comment:
config.json -- input to solenoid3d.py.

    Layout:
      experiment  : global experiment metadata
      physics     : shared physics (gravity, mass, air drag, magnet properties)
      mesh        : mesh sizes
      geometry    : air-domain extents
      curves      : LIST of curve blocks, ONE per body geometry. To add a new
                    curve, simply add another named entry under [curves]. Each
                    block must carry:  label, color, z_release_m, N_turns,
                    R_load_ohm, damping_extra_N_s_per_m, body_name, sif_suffix.
                    Wire-related keys (wire_diameter_m,
                    wire_conductivity_S_per_m) are read when N_turns > 0.

experiment.name: magnet_spring_oscillator
experiment._comment_mode: motion_mode selects which law drives the mesh: 'spring' uses config.json -> [spring] (damped harmonic oscillator), 'free_fall' uses z = z0 - 1/2 g t^2. Both are PRESCRIBED translations applied by RigidMeshMapper.
experiment.description: Permanent cylindrical magnet suspended on a spring above a coil, released from rest and oscillating through the coil bore. We track trajectory, flux, EMF, induced current and the Lenz braking force for multiple coil configurations.
experiment._comment_time: t_end_default_s spans TWO full spring periods (T ~= 0.2995 s). dt must stay small: the RigidMeshMapper tracks a prescribed translation accurately only when the per-step displacement (here A*omega0*dt ~= 0.84 mm) is well below the local element size. make_sif.py turns these two into `Timestep Sizes` / `Timestep Intervals`.

magnet._comment: Permanent NdFeB cylinder.  CAREFUL: `H_mag_m` is the HALF height used by the on-axis dipole formula; the real extent is z1_m - z0_m = 0.030 m.  The mesh position equals the spring RELEASE position, so the prescribed displacement starts at exactly zero.

coil._comment: Coil/bore body geometry as built by solenoid3d.py (S_IN/S_OUT/S_Z0/S_Z1). Used by the oscilloscope to integrate the flux through the winding.

spring._comment:
SPRING-MASS-DAMPER experiment (replaces the free-fall motion law).

    The magnet hangs from a helical spring whose top is fixed to a clamped
    anchor plate above the coil.  Instead of the free-fall law z = z0 - g t^2
    the mesh is driven with the analytic damped-oscillator solution:

        m z'' = -m g - k (L - L0) - c z' - F_lenz
        z(t)  = z_eq + A e^(-gamma t) [cos(wd t) + (gamma/wd) sin(wd t)]

    with      omega0 = sqrt(k/m)
              gamma  = c / (2 m)
              wd     = sqrt(omega0^2 - gamma^2)
              sag    = m g / k              (static stretch)
              L_eq   = anchor_z0 - (z_eq + H_mag/2)
              L0     = L_eq - sag           (unstretched length)
              A      = |z_release - z_eq|   (released from rest)

    All lengths are in metres, angles in radians.  The MESH represents the
    spring at its EQUILIBRIUM length; the oscillation is a prescribed
    translation (RigidMeshMapper + Mesh Translate 3 = MATC expression),
    exactly like the free-fall case, so no rigid-body solver is needed.

    NOTE: the spring (R = 6..8 mm) sits on the axis INSIDE the coil bore and
    is non-magnetic (mu_r = 1), so it has NO effect on the field.  Meshing it
    is therefore optional -- see include_in_mesh.
spring._comment_anchor: Clamped plate the spring hangs from.  Its bottom face (anchor_z0) is the fixed end of the spring.
spring._comment_spring_geom: Spring = hollow tube at its EQUILIBRIUM length.  spring_z1 is welded to the anchor bottom; spring_z0 would touch the magnet top if the magnet sat at z_eq.
spring._comment_derived: Recomputed by solenoid3d.py / oscilloscope.py from the values above -- do NOT edit by hand; they are recorded here only so the defaults are self-documenting.

mesh._comment: Sizes are applied to the corner POINTS of each volume (required with General.ExpertMode=1). The magnet and coil are refined locally; the far-field air stays coarse. The TRANSIENT run performs one direct linear solve per timestep, so the total node count directly drives wall-clock time.

empty._comment: REFERENCE -- no conductor at all. Free-fall baseline (no Lenz braking, no induced current).
empty.label: 空 (无导体)

copper_closed._comment: 铜线闭路 CLOSED CIRCUIT, copper. 50 turns of 0.7 mm Cu wire (sigma=5.96e7) into a 10 ohm load. Current flows -> EMF/R, Lenz braking and Joule loss.
copper_closed.label: 铜线闭路 (Cu 50t 0.7mm, R=10Ω)

aluminum_closed._comment: 铝线闭路 CLOSED CIRCUIT, aluminium. Same 50 turns / 0.7 mm but sigma=3.5e7, so R_wire is 1.70x the copper value (0.527 vs 0.310 ohm) into the same 10 ohm load.
aluminum_closed.label: 铝线闭路 (Al 50t 0.7mm, R=10Ω)

aluminum_open._comment: 铝线开路 OPEN CIRCUIT, aluminium. Same winding but R_load=inf: the EMF still appears across the terminals, I = 0, therefore NO Lenz braking. Compare against aluminum_closed to isolate the circuit-state effect.
aluminum_open.label: 铝线开路 (Al 50t 0.7mm, R=∞)
